extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications licensees, auction participants, small business advocates, and regulatory analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Mapping and applying SBA small business size definitions and FCC auction small/very small/entrepreneur classifications across spectrum services and industries, and explaining how those definitions affect auction eligibility (bidding credits/installment payments) and Commission analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active licenses vs. number of licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of active licenses does not equate to the number of licensees; a licensee can have one or more licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly when reporting license counts and when estimating how many licensees might qualify as small entities; cautions against using active license counts as a proxy for number of businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-auction business-size tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission does not generally track subsequent business size unless, in the context of assignments or transfers, unjust enrichment issues are implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why the number of winning bidders that qualify as small businesses at the close of an auction does not necessarily represent the number of small businesses currently in service; informs limits of Commission's ability to estimate current small-entity counts after auctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission limitation on employee data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission does not collect data on the number of employees for licensees providing many services, so it is not able to estimate the number of licensees with active licenses that would qualify as small under the SBA’s small business size standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This data limitation recurs across multiple service categories and constrains the Commission's SBA-based small-entity estimates; where employee data are absent the Commission commonly relies on SBA/NAICS mappings or other proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NAICS industry mapping to apply SBA size standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For each service the Commission identifies the closest industry (NAICS) with an SBA small business size standard (for example, 'Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)' NAICS 517312).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the basis for applying SBA employee or receipts thresholds to particular radio services when estimating how many licensees qualify as small entities; citations to specific NAICS definitions and CFR sections are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband PCS auction small business definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In auctions for these licenses, the Commission defined 'small business' as an entity that, together with its affiliates and controlling interests, has average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million for the preceding three years, and a 'very small business' as an entity that, together with its affiliates and controlling interests, has had average annual gross revenues not exceeding $15 million for the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classifications were used for eligibility for bidding credits and installment payments in Broadband PCS auctions; cited Auctions 4,5,10,11,22,35,58,71,78 as contexts where winning bidders claiming small business credits won licenses in specific blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMR (Specialized Mobile Radio) SBA standard (NAICS mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: SMR services are mapped to 'Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)' (NAICS 517312), for which the SBA size standard classifies a business as small if it has 1,500 or fewer employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission cites U.S. Census Bureau data and Universal Service Monitoring Report counts to estimate that the vast majority of SMR providers/licensees have 1,500 or fewer employees and thus can be considered small, while noting classification caveats and data limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower 700 MHz auction small business categories
rubrics_metrics.description: For Lower 700 MHz Band license auctions the Commission adopted criteria for three groups of small businesses: a 'very small business' (average annual gross revenues not exceeding $15 million for the preceding three years), a 'small business' (average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million for the preceding three years), and an 'entrepreneur' (average gross revenues not exceeding $3 million for the preceding three years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions were applied for bidding credits and installment payment eligibility; the Commission cites auction results showing numbers of winning bidders claiming these classifications and the licenses they won.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper 700 MHz auction small business definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For Upper 700 MHz Band auctions, the Commission defined a 'small business' as an entity that, together with its affiliates and controlling principals, has average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million for the preceding three years, and a 'very small business' as an entity with average gross revenues not more than $15 million for the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine bidding credit/installment payment eligibility; the report cites auction outcomes (e.g., three very small business winners won five of twelve licenses) as examples of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-Ground Radiotelephone Service SBA and auction definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The closest SBA industry is 'Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)' (small = 1,500 or fewer employees). For auctions of Air-Ground Radiotelephone Service licenses, the Commission defined 'small business' as average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million for the preceding three years and 'very small business' as average annual gross revenues not exceeding $15 million for the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes permitted operations in the service and that in the relevant auction neither of the two winning bidders claimed small business status; cites 47 CFR § 22.99 and auction fact sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3650–3700 MHz band SBA mapping and absence of a specific standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Wireless broadband services in the 3650–3700 MHz band fall within the 'Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)' industry (SBA small = 1,500 or fewer employees). The Commission has not developed a small business size standard applicable specifically to 3650–3700 MHz licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission estimates, based on granted licenses, that the majority of licensees are small ISPs; cites number of active licenses (902 as of Nov 2021) and again notes lack of employee data prevents precise SBA-based counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed Microwave Services SBA mapping and auction credit availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed microwave services are mapped to 'Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)' (small = 1,500 or fewer employees). When bidding credits are adopted for auctions of fixed microwave frequency bands, such credits may be available to small, very small, and entrepreneur entities based on average gross revenues pursuant to the competitive bidding rules and Part 101 rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the various fixed microwave service types (UMFUS, millimeter wave, LMDS, DEMS, 24 GHz, MAS, MVDDS) and cites the specific CFR sections where auction/credit rules are established (e.g., 47 CFR §§ 101.538, 101.1112, 101.1319, 101.1429).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband Radio Service (BRS) auction classifications (entrepreneur/very small/small)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the auction of BRS licenses the Commission adopted three groups: an 'entrepreneur' (average gross revenues not exceeding $3 million for the preceding three years), a 'very small business' (average annual gross revenues exceed $3 million and did not exceed $15 million for the preceding three years), and a 'small business' (average gross revenues exceed $15 million and did not exceed $40 million for the preceding three years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories determined eligibility for bidding credits and installment payments; the document cites auction 86 results showing how many winning bidders claimed each classification and the licenses won.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational Broadband Service (EBS) small business definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: EBS small business definitions: a 'small business' is an entity that, together with its affiliates and controlling interests, has average gross revenues not more than $55 million for the preceding five years; a 'very small business' is an entity with average gross revenues not more than $20 million for the preceding five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds are specific to EBS auctions; the Commission reiterates the usual caveats about auction winners vs. current in-service status and lack of employee data for precise SBA-based estimates. (See 47 CFR § 27.1219(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Satellite Telecommunications SBA receipts standard (NAICS 517410)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 'Satellite Telecommunications' (NAICS 517410), the SBA small business size standard classifies a business with $35 million or less in annual receipts as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission cites 2017 Census data and the Universal Service Monitoring Report (65 providers reporting satellite telecommunications in 2021) to estimate that a little more than half of such providers can be considered small under the SBA receipts standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Other Telecommunications SBA receipts standard (NAICS 517919)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'All Other Telecommunications' industry (NAICS 517919) has an SBA small business size standard classifying firms with annual receipts of $35 million or less as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Census data for 2017 are cited (1,079 firms, 1,039 with revenue < $25M) to support the Commission's estimate that the majority of firms in this industry are small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable and Other Subscription Programming SBA receipts standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Census Bureau industry 'Cable and Other Subscription Programming' has an SBA small business size standard classifying firms with annual receipts less than $41.5 million as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Census 2017 figures (378 firms; breakdown of revenues) are cited to justify the Commission's estimate that a majority of firms in this industry are small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small cable company definition for rate regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of cable rate regulation, the Commission defines a 'small cable company' as one serving 400,000 or fewer subscribers nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a Commission-specific small-entity standard (distinct from SBA receipts or employee thresholds) used for rate regulation analyses; referenced in the Commission's cable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SBA thresholds to determine auction eligibility (bidding credits/installment payments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Across many services, the Commission's small business size standards (whether SBA employee/receipt standards or auction-specific gross-revenue thresholds) are used to determine eligibility for bidding credits and installment payments in spectrum license auctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the functional purpose of the various small/very small/entrepreneur definitions cited throughout the document; multiple auctions and fact sheets are cited as examples of application (Auctions 44, 49, 60, 73, 86, etc.).
